Prevalence Profile Along a Protein

Source: R/delta_plots.R
profile_plot.Rd

Plot every library peptide of the selected proteins at its position in the protein (x-axis) and at its prevalence in each group (y-axis), one panel per protein. The plot shows where along a protein the reactivity sits and how it differs between groups. The proteins are the ones passed in proteins; a shaded band marks the longest run of overlapping significant peptides, and DELTA statistics from compute_delta() can be added to the panel titles.

Usage

profile_plot(
  prev_tbl,
  proteins,
  groups = NULL,
  peplib = NULL,
  show_overlap = TRUE,
  alpha = 0.05,
  delta_tbl = NULL,
  custom_colors = NULL,
  ncol = NULL,
  line_width_pt = 0.9,
  plot_title = NULL,
  plot_subtitle = NULL,
  x_label = NULL,
  y_label = NULL
)

Arguments

prev_tbl

Data frame from compute_pop() (or equivalent) with columns feature, group1, group2, prop1, prop2 and, for show_overlap, p_raw. If it has a rank column, only the "peptide_id" rows are used; a group_col column, if present, separates group pairs.

proteins

Character vector of protein_seq_id values, one panel each, in this order. Names, if given, are used as panel titles; otherwise the title is the protein's annotation and ID.

groups

Optional character vector of the groups to draw, in legend order. Names, if given, are used as legend labels. Defaults to all groups in prev_tbl, pair by pair in the order of its rows.

peplib

Optional peptide library with columns peptide_id, protein_seq_id, pos, aa_seq, len_seq and taxon_with_protein_unique_annotation. If NULL, the phiperio peptide libraries the peptide IDs belong to are detected from their prefixes and fetched with get_peptide_library().

show_overlap

Logical; shade the longest run of overlapping hit peptides per protein, group pair and direction (see Details). Default TRUE.

alpha

Numeric in (0, 1]; BH-adjusted p-value threshold for hit peptides. Default 0.05.

delta_tbl

Optional data frame from compute_delta() run with rank_cols = "protein_seq_id", with columns feature, group1, group2, T_obs and p_perm.

custom_colors

Optional vector of group colors, named by group or recycled in groups order. Defaults to phip_palette.

ncol

Number of panel columns, passed to ggplot2::facet_wrap().

line_width_pt

Line width of the peptide segments. Default 0.9.

plot_title, plot_subtitle

Optional plot labels.

x_label, y_label

Optional axis labels.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

Each peptide is a horizontal segment from its first to its last amino acid (pos + 1 to pos + nchar(aa_seq), clipped at the protein length len_seq), drawn at its prevalence in each group. All library peptides of a protein are drawn: peptides missing from prev_tbl are drawn at 0\ Peptides without a position in the library are left out.

Group prevalences are read from both sides of the group pairs in prev_tbl, so a table with several pairs, e.g. from compute_pop(group_cols = c("control_vs_sjogren", "control_vs_sle")), gives one line per group. A group that appears in several pairs must have the same prevalences in all of them.

With show_overlap = TRUE, hit peptides are those with a BH-adjusted p_raw of at most alpha, the correction running over all peptides of a group pair in prev_tbl. For each protein, group pair and direction (the group with the higher prevalence), the hit peptides form runs: a run grows with every next hit peptide that overlaps the region it covers so far. The longest run is shaded in the colour of the group with the higher prevalence when it has at least two peptides. Bands are drawn only for pairs whose two groups are both drawn.

With delta_tbl, each panel title lists every group pair tested for the protein, with the DELTA statistic T_obs and the permutation p-value p_perm; proteins without a row are marked "not tested".

Examples

peplib <- data.frame(
  peptide_id     = paste0("pep", 1:6),
  protein_seq_id = rep(c("protA", "protB"), each = 3),
  pos            = c(0, 20, 40, 0, 25, 50),
  aa_seq         = strrep("A", 30),
  len_seq        = rep(c(70, 75), each = 3),
  taxon_with_protein_unique_annotation =
    rep(c("Species a: protein A", "Species b: protein B"), each = 3)
)
prev_tbl <- data.frame(
  rank    = "peptide_id",
  feature = rep(c("pep1", "pep2", "pep4", "pep5"), 2),
  group1  = "control",
  group2  = rep(c("sjogren", "sle"), each = 4),
  prop1   = rep(c(0.10, 0.20, 0.05, 0.00), 2),
  prop2   = c(0.40, 0.50, 0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.60, 0.00, 0.10),
  p_raw   = c(0.001, 0.002, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.001, 0.5, 0.5)
)

# pep1 and pep2 overlap and are both more common in sjogren: one band
profile_plot(prev_tbl, proteins = c("protA", "protB"), peplib = peplib)


# two groups with display labels, DELTA statistics in the panel titles
delta_tbl <- data.frame(
  rank    = "protein_seq_id",
  feature = "protA",
  group1  = "control",
  group2  = c("sjogren", "sle"),
  T_obs   = c(3.1, 1.2),
  p_perm  = c(0.002, 0.21)
)
profile_plot(
  prev_tbl,
  proteins  = c("Protein A" = "protA", "Protein B" = "protB"),
  groups    = c(Controls = "control", "Sjogren" = "sjogren"),
  peplib    = peplib,
  delta_tbl = delta_tbl
)
